narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Anyeint originated as a royal court dance performed by women.
Following the 1885 fall of the Konbaung dynasty, it moved into the public domain, becoming a popular hybrid of dance and comedy for the merchant class.
The first troupe was formed in Mandalay around 1900 by U Chit Phwe and Ma Sein Thone.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Anyeint is a form of light entertainment.
Historically, it served as a venue for political satire and social commentary, though modern performances are subject to strict censorship by the Myanmar Motion Picture Enterprise.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The performance centers on the anyeint minthami, who performs solo and group dances to instrumental music.
Comedians provide slapstick routines while the actress changes costumes.
The dance is characterized by the minthami's interaction with the comedians, who provide improvised jokes and insults that the dancer must rebut.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Performers wear costumes identical to those seen in traditional Burmese marionette theater.
Comedians typically wear checkered-patterned Taungshay-style longyi (sarongs) and loose coats, a style innovated by U Po Sein.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Key figures include U Chit Phwe and Ma Sein Thone (founders of the first troupe), U Po Sein (costume innovator), Zarganar (comedian), and actresses like May Than Nu and Yadana Khin.
Anyeint is a form of pwe (traditional Burmese entertainment) and evolved from royal court dance traditions.

music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of Anyeint (Myanmar). Instruments: pattala (xylophone). Vocal style: Singing interspersed with comedic dialogue.. Form: Sequence of solo and group dances accompanied by instrumental music.. Mood: light, theatrical, comedic. It should sound like this: A small all-male orchestra led by the xylophone, accompanying a lead singer/dancer with rhythmic instrumental music and vocal segments. New melody, new arrangement: do not quote or imitate any specific recorded song; keep the idiom, the instruments, the pulse and the proportions.

tracks.use: chapters: dance it to the music

rules: Original composition only — no sampling, no melody of any existing recording, no lyrics from any song.
Traditional public-domain tunes may be used only when the profile names them and a public-domain source is on file; otherwise compose new material in the idiom.
Keep the proportions true: the meter, the tempo range and the instrument roles the sources describe.
Label every generated track with the tool, the date and this brief, so provenance is always clear.
